summary: The isPanicking() function calls runtime.Callers() and runtime.CallersFrames() on every workflow coroutine yield to detect panics, consuming 14.3% CPU and 10.2% memory allocations under load.
userImpact: Users experience significantly reduced workflow throughput and higher resource utilization under load due to excessive CPU and memory consumption from panic detection.
rootCause: isPanicking() unconditionally calls runtime.Callers() and runtime.CallersFrames() on every coroutine yield point, causing stack unwinding and allocations (81MB uintptr arrays, 125MB frame iterators, 48MB frame copies).
proposedFix: Use recover() to detect panics, set a goroutine-local flag when entering panic handling, or allow disabling via WorkerOptions.
keyQuote: This single function accounts for 14.3% of total CPU time and 10.2% of total allocations under load, dominated by stack unwinding.
